item.title: Cowboys news: Young defenders made mistakes, “critical” improvements needed
item.description: Here is today’s Dallas Cowboys news.
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys week one defensive performance did not feel at all like the “graduation” Christian Parker said it should be, and now young players and veterans alike will have to get back in the classroom and learn quickly before another NFC East battle against the Washington Commanders.

Quinnen Williams was vocal after the loss about the accountability this defense will have to get better, but they will also be spending this week sorting out who can fill in for Malik Hooker and DeMarvion Overshown who were injured against the Giants.

Schottenheimer: Cowboys’ young defenders ‘need to learn quickly’ after Giants’ lesson – Todd Brock, The Cowboys Wire

It was trial by fire for a ton of new faces in the Cowboys defensive lineup, and frankly one they were not ready for.

Schottenheimer acknowledged the inexperience as part of the reason for such breakdowns.

“Not an excuse, guys: we did not play well, but you’ve got young players,” he said. “A young player closes and Jaxson Dart boots and gets outside. We don’t push three different times to the [expletive] flat route, excuse my language. Those are going to happen, and we have to coach the young players better. But when you play young players, it’s part of the deal. And they need to learn quickly.”

Quinnen Williams: We really need to be critical to get better – Josh Alper, Pro Football Talk

The Cowboys got pushed around in the trenches, and Quinnen Williams is taking accountability.

“I think we definitely gotta be critical [of ourselves] in our approach, when we get to [preparing for Week 2]. And it’s a great week to learn, and to get things better,” Williams said, via the team’s website. “The guys we got in our locker room, especially on defense, are unbelievable when it comes down to taking constructive criticism and accountability, first of all, and let’s move,” he said. “We had a lot of mental errors, a lot of busts today, and just really need to be critical with that going into this week; and focus on getting better.”

Malik Hooker, DeMarvion Overshown to miss a couple weeks with injuries – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com

The Dallas defense comes out of Week 1 with major concerns at linebacker and safety after losing starters to injury at both positions.

After saying following Dallas’ 28-20 loss to New York that initial tests showed a fractured forearm for Malik Hooker, Schottenheimer confirmed Hooker did in fact suffer a fracture in his forearm. He will have surgery on Tuesday.

“It sounds like it’s one that doesn’t require as long a period of time [to recover]. So we’re hoping it’s a two week window.” Schottenheimer said.

As for Overshown, Schottenheimer said Sunday night he wasn’t sure the extent of his hamstring injury. That ended up being a strain, and Schottenheimer said it could be “one to two weeks as well” to recover from.

3 Cowboys Week 1 Takeaways: We Got Eberflused on Defense – Cody Warren, Inside The Star

Cowboys fans are left wondering when the defense will ever look and feel any different at 0-1 for the second straight year.

Dallas changed coordinators, but Sunday night wasn’t any different than last season under Matt Eberflus. No pressure, broken coverage, and mistake after mistake.

Jaxson Dart dissected the defense, found his tight end, Isaiah Likely, so many times it felt like he was the only receiver on the field. On top of that, Dallas couldn’t keep Dart in the pocket. I felt like Dart could’ve had 10 yards running anytime he wanted.

The Dallas Cowboys’ defense showed way too many flaws in Week 1, but there’s a worrisome one that’s close to unfixable – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports

The Cowboys need another big time pass rusher in the worst way.

In 20 plays rushing the passer with four players only, the Cowboys recorded two QB pressures, according to NextGen Stats.

It was their lowest pressure rate since 2021. When the Cowboys did blitz, the Giants usually had the right answer. Whether it was Dart taking off himself or him finding an open target down the field.

Tyler Guyton a bright spot in Cowboys’ demoralizing loss – Matthew Holleran, Blogging The Boys

The Cowboys were able to trust Tyler Guyton on an island for a lot of snaps at left tackle, as his improvement is encouraging.

While facing off against star pass rusher Brian Burns, the 25-year-old tackle allowed no pressures across 20 pass-blocking matchups. On the night as a whole, Guyton allowed just two pressures in his 36 total pass blocks in the game, a very solid mark going up against a talented Giants’ pass rush.

This performance is even more impressive when you consider that Guyton did not have his usual running mate, All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith, lining up next to him every play.

item.title: New York Jets News: Week 1 Results Deliver Gift For Jets
item.description: Your daily links to the New York Jets
item.content:encoded:
We are still feeling the high of a New York Jets victory on a Tuesday, but that isn’t the only thing we’re celebrating.

Over the weekend, all of the moons and stars aligned for the green and white. The Jets won, the Dallas Cowboys lost, the Green Bay Packers lost, and the Indianapolis Colts lost.

The Jets control their own first-round pick, the Colts’ first-rounder, and whichever pick ends up being worse between America’s Team and the Cheeseheads. So every time the Colts, Cowboys, and Packers lose, that’s excellent news for the Jets.

The fan base can often be divided by the pro-tankers and the optimists. If we aren’t winning the Super Bowl, some fans have argued that tanking, losing on purpose, will better serve the team long-term because of the potential promised prince QB that can help turn everything around in the draft.

Well, this year the arguments should die down. Why? I’m glad you asked, random person reading this article, because the Jets can have the best of both worlds.

They can be competitive, win games, saving Aaron Glenn’s job in the process, while also getting that prized college QB, whoever that may be. Instead of rooting for the Jets to lose, root for the Colts/Packers/Cowboys to bite the dust.

We have enough people fighting against us on a day-to-day basis; we don’t need to fight each other.

item.title: Kyle Williams among Patriots ready to step up after A.J. Brown injury
item.description: A.J. Brown is set to be out at least the next four weeks.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots are set to be without star wide receiver A.J. Brown for at least the next month after he landed on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain.

It’s a significant loss for the Patriots’ passing attack, but one that will not force the team to overhaul its offensive approach. Instead, New England will count on a group effort to replace its top wideout.

“I mean, we’re trying to install here and putting guys in spots that are best for them and best for us. And so, I don’t know how much we want to tweak things,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “We’ll go through our game plan, and just like we did when A.J. was out there – sometimes he was the X, sometimes he was the F, the Z. You know what I mean? We’ll have to move guys around to different positions.”

Among those that is expected to see an increase in playing time is second-year wide receiver Kyle Williams, who played 12 snaps in the opener, mostly in relief of Brown in the second half.

“We want to get Kyle involved. I’ve tried to talk about that,” Vrabel said. “I’m hopeful that Kyle can find a role for us and find a way to help us, using his speed and catch and run opportunities like we saw last year at times or some shot-type plays.”

In his limited Week 1 action, Williams was not targeted by Drake Maye. But moving forward, a more “locked-in” and “focused” Williams is ready to take on a bigger role now that he has a better understanding of Josh McDaniels’ offense in his second season.

And while his big-play ability was on display last season and this preseason, he knows he has more to offer in that role.

“A lot. I mean, if I wanted to really go, I’d give you a Christmas list, for real,” Williams said. “But I can do a lot, man. And just when those opportunities present itself, that’s when I’ll be able to show it. But I know I’m more than just speed.”

Veteran Mack Hollins will also continue to see more opportunities come his way. Hollins led all Patriots wide receivers with 50 snaps in Week 1 while also leading the team with 51 receiving yards 

“Mack’s always taking advantage of his opportunities. I think that the quarterback knows he’s going to be in the right spot when he’s supposed to be there,” Vrabel said. “Mack’s been through that a lot, and we’re comfortable being able to move him around as well in those multiple positions.”

The Patriots will also need more from free-agent addition Romeo Doubs.

In his Patriots debut, Doubs finished with zero catches across his three targets. Doubs has a bad drop on a wide-open pass that proceeded an interception, while another target in his direction was also picked off. Still, his head coach is not losing any faith.

“He dropped a pass. You know what I mean? Guys, everybody drops a pass. Everybody misses a tackle,” Vrabel said. “You talk to him the same way you always talk to him. Figure out a way to make a play to help us win, and he did a lot of great things during camp, just like everybody did. And so, I know he’s excited to get back out there, get to work and to find a way to help us win.”

While the Patriots wide receiver room — which also includes Efton Chism III — is a deep group, removing Brown from the equation will be a significant loss to overcome. The star receiver started strong in the opener, recording three catches for 26 yards while drawing a 40-plus-yard pass interference penalty to set up the team’s first score.

“Everybody’s disappointed for him, and he’s disappointed,” Vrabel said. “He wants to play. He’s a competitor, and we’ll have to get him back as quickly as possible. Obviously at a four-game window, and make sure that he’s ready to go mentally and physically when he does get back.”

Brown’s high-ankle sprain is reportedly expected to keep him out closer to six weeks. While the team is hoping for a speedy recovery, the receiver group is ready to pick up the slack in the meantime.

“Just hoping for a speedy recovery, get him back on the field, because we definitely do need him. But I mean, one man down is the next man up,” Williams said. “I think that’s everybody’s mentality in every room. So, we just got to keep approaching how we’ve been approaching it from the spring all the way up until now, and just hopefully nothing really changes or alters what we’re trying to do.”
